identity.realm: The eleventh gate, reached on a suspended load of two chemistries and stopped there. The sac is shallower than a saltfolk's and still dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel behind it is still split and a frame that can stand in the mixture is a frame that cannot be filled all the way at once. Range is not power, and he is the standing proof of that sentence on the only piece of ground where both halves of it are the same job.

appearance.presentation: A wiry, weather-tanned man who is never dry and never quite still wet. In a room of saltfolk he is the one whose boots are damp; in a room of tidecallers he is the one whose sleeves carry a white bloom. Nobody can guess what he last drank, and he has stopped trying to guess it himself. He carries a flat wooden rake that he uses as a pointer, a staff and, on bad ground, an anchor.
appearance.age: Forty-one. A brinecaller spans longer than a saltfolk and shorter than a tidecaller, and he has no intention of finding out where the line falls; his working life began at nine and the arithmetic of the section has been counting on him for thirty-two years, which is most of what a body like his has.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame that never finished hardening: narrow through the shoulders, long in the forearm, with the ankles thickened from three decades of standing in a fluid that would strip the skin off anything else. The sac across his spine is shallow and sits high, and because the penetrating vessel behind it is still split he has never once been able to pressurise both flanks at the same time. He is built to stand in one place for a long time, which is the only thing he is ever asked to do.
appearance.complexion: Salt-stiffened across the shoulders and forearms and soft everywhere else, because the mixture dries on him at different rates in different places. Around the mouth and the eyes the skin stays damp and faintly translucent. He flushes faintly and unevenly after a shift and returns to grey within the hour, and people who have only met him indoors assume the colour is excitement.
appearance.hair: Bleached to straw on top and dark and wet at the nape, because the crown dries in the wind off the floor and the nape never does. He wears it long enough to get a handful of it wet when he tests a wall, and short enough that he can hear it moving, which he treats as a practical fact rather than a vanity.
appearance.eyes: The best chemical sense in the record, and it shows mainly in what he does with them: he reads a surface rather than looking at it, and he looks away when he is thinking. His eyes are pale and water-clear and completely ordinary, which is why nobody believes the reading until it is too late to argue.
appearance.palette: Wet white, pale brine green, and rust. The mixture he walks is the colour of a wet coin and it dries to a chalk crust on his hems; the only saturated note in any frame is the rust bleeding out of the header wall he has leaned on for thirty years. His clothes are never a single value because the section dries in bands across him, and the bands are the most honest thing about his appearance.
appearance.attire: A short coat of oiled sacking cut above the knee so it can be stripped and hung without being peeled, sleeves laced tight to the wrist to keep the mixture out, and a hood that stays down because a hood that goes up on the floor is a hood full of brine. Heavy boots cut for standing still rather than walking. Everything he wears is a thing that can be taken off in a doorway, because he has learned what happens to clothing that cannot.
appearance.marks: A pale band across each wrist where the mixture has been sitting for thirty years and has not been allowed to, and a white crust in the creases of both elbows that no amount of scrubbing reaches. Below the ribs on the left side, a long smooth ridge under the skin: the sac, shallower than a saltfolk's and still dorsal to the spine, sitting exactly where the vessel splits and refusing, after thirty-two years, to pressurise on both sides at once.
appearance.bearing: Weighted and square while he is on the floor and light everywhere else. He stops dead instead of adjusting when a reading changes, which reads to an outsider like indecision and is in fact the only trained response the section permits.

canon.role_in_story: The Brine Reach is a dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline, because the basin's brine is the one supply that never fails and the specialised body that can drink it stops above the brine line, so the population cannot be moved up the shore without ceasing to be the people it governs. Between the header and the crystallising floor there is a stretch where the flood and the pan are in the same room and neither has won, and that stretch has to be walked and raked while it is still mixed, because the moment it resolves the salt comes out wrong and a season is lost. A saltfolk body cannot stand in it. A tidecaller body can stand in it and must leave it within the hour. He is the man the reach sends in, and he is paid by the shift, so his standing is measured in hours and the number is always falling. The dominion classifies its people by the depth of water they may moor at, which is one measurement of one body of water; he is the only man in the dispute whose body is two of them, which makes him the one party who can simply walk off it and the only man nobody can move.
canon.first_appearance: First seen coming out of the header channel to the thigh with the rake still in one hand, stopping at the channel edge rather than on the bank, and refusing the cup of fresh water held out to him until he has stood in the sun long enough for the mixture to leave him by evaporation instead of by drinking. He answers the question of why he will not drink by asking what the cup was drawn from.
canon.lore: A brinecaller is the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, produced by crossing the salt-adapted people with the fully watered ones, and it exists because both parents are trapped by their own element and the cross is the single biological answer to being trapped twice. That answer is a merchant, which is why the crossing spread. What the crossing actually bought the reach is not trade but a worker: a saltfolk frame carrying a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus, with dermal intake, a wider electrolyte tolerance and a kidney that reads two chemistries at once. Its ceiling is the eleventh gate, inherited from the salt parent and unmoved by the cross, because the sac is still dorsal to the spine and the penetrating vessel behind it is still split, so a frame that could stand in the mixture is a frame that cannot be filled all the way at once. Range is not power, and the section is the only place in the setting where that sentence is a job description. His discipline is the deliberate opposite of banking: he keeps the two chemistries suspended in the sac together on purpose, because a body that holds an undefined mass has to carry more of it and recovers faster than a frame that has resolved itself into one thing. There is no version of him that is neutral. Every cup of either water is a move toward an end he cannot undo, which is why he does not drink on the floor and why the reach has stopped giving him work that would let him. Nobody has ever asked him what he is, and the honest answer has never fit in a field.
history: Put into the header channel at nine as a reader, on the ground that a child's readings were less trusted than an adult's and a child's mistake cost a field rather than a season, and walked into the mixed section for the first time at nineteen, at which point his own readings stopped agreeing with the depth book and had to be arbitrated by somebody older.

Worked out at twenty-one that a walker's competence has a half-life of one shift, and that the only variable under his control was what he drank, and adopted the rule of not drinking on the floor, which he has broken exactly twice and can name both.

Learned the suspended load at twenty-four, which means carrying a mass of two chemistries that have not been allowed to precipitate and never paying it out of qi, and cleared the eleventh gate on it four years later and stopped there, because the vessel behind the sac is still split and the salt parent stopped at the same gate a hundred years before him.

Was measured against the depth book after a season in which the basin's level rose, and was reclassified to a depth he cannot be moored at, on the grounds that the book records one water and his is two, and has been reclassified twice since for the same reason.

Refused, at thirty-six, a post on the flood side of the reach where the reach would have had to classify him by a single chemistry, and has been living on mixed shifts rather than on the flood-side rate ever since, which everyone involved understands and nobody has put in writing.

personality.summary: Slow, methodical and privately exact about a measurement nobody has ever asked him to keep. He reads a mixture the way other people read a face and has never been able to explain the skill to anybody who did not grow up standing in it, so he has developed a way of demonstrating it that looks like stubbornness.
traits: patient well past what the work requires, because the work rewards nobody who is early
scrupulous about the order of operations to a degree that has been mistaken for superstition and has never once been wrong
completely incurious about his own comfort and demonstrably curious about everybody else's reading
deeply hostile to being praised in advance of the result
mannerisms: lays the flat of his own forearm on a surface and lifts it before he will believe a reading
does not drink anything at all while he is on the floor, and will not say why in front of people he has just met
walks the header wall with his shoulder because the wall reports the flow before his eyes do
stops dead the instant a reading changes rather than correcting toward it
answers a question about a number with a procedure, and a question about a person with a number
motivations: to be classified by something he can measure instead of by a figure the reach assigns him each season
to reach the flood side on his own terms or to stay where he is for the rest of his life
to be the reason the section is walked by a person rather than by a rule somebody wrote once
flaws: cannot say no to a shift that needs walking, and cannot be cured of it by rest
has never told his household what a shift actually costs him, so his household has an arithmetic that is wrong and cannot be corrected from outside
treats his own deterioration as a schedule rather than as a decline, and has been wrong about that for six years
personality.voice: Few words, nearly all of them procedural. He names a measurement where another person would name a feeling. The only time his manner changes at all is when somebody describes the water as a single thing, and then he goes very quiet and asks which one they meant.
taboos: drinking on the floor, under any pressure, including his own
quoting a standing weight out loud, or hearing one quoted and not objecting
describing the section in terms of salt alone
letting anybody else read his forearm

relationships.note: A saltfolk frame with a shallower sac and a tidecaller's sensory apparatus, metabolising brine and fresh water alike, and it exists because both parents are trapped by their own element. Its ceiling is the eleventh gate and it never moved, because the sac is still dorsal to the spine: the cross widened what he can reach and did not raise what he can hold, and the section is the only place where those two facts are the same job.

A dominion whose territory is exactly its waterline, because the basin's brine never fails and the body that can drink it stops above the brine line. He is the reach's answer to the reach's own geography, and the reach pays him by the shift, so the only figure anybody keeps about him is a number that falls.

A household's standing is the depth of water it may moor at and the basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment shrinks without anybody having done anything. A depth is one measurement of one body of water, and his body is two of them, which makes him the only party to the dispute who can simply leave it and the only one nobody can move.

It trains the body to keep a larger share of its load so that less of each effort has to be paid for out of qi. Every other practitioner on the tier is keeping a share of a burden; he is the burden, and the discipline is the only reason thirty-two years of standing in a mixture has not finished him.

A stance that spends the whole body's weight instead of its speed so that the practitioner cannot be moved while it is held. He holds it in the section for four hours at a stretch. If he is pushed, the mixture resolves where he is standing and a season's salt comes out wrong, which makes the one drill he takes seriously the only discipline in the setting whose failure is measured in somebody else's year.

The only watercourse on the tier that is not brine, and its bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement standing on it. He is the one body in the setting that can sit out a dry season on pan brine and then drink the flood, so the run's schedule feeds him rather than evicting him, and that is why the reach's routes bend toward his section rather than past it.

reference_stats.summary: He carries what no other body on the tier can hold: two chemistries at once, deliberately, without letting either of them win. He is the strongest worker in the mixed section by a margin nobody argues about and the least replaceable man in the reach by an enormous margin, and both facts are the same fact. He has no defence worth naming against anything that happens on dry ground, and he is at his best in the one place on the setting where a man cannot be hurried and cannot leave.
strengths: holds an undefined mass in the sac without either chemistry precipitating, which is the only reason a person can stand in the mixed section at all
reads the concentration of any water by laying a hand on it, with no instrument and no second reading, and has been wrong in front of witnesses twice in thirty-two years
keeps a far larger share of an effort in the body than the frame it sits on, so a four-hour hold costs him nothing that a two-hour hold would cost an ordinary man
cannot be moved while the stance is held, which in the section is the same as being immovable to the one thing that could move him
works both halves of a shoreline's year without dying at either end of it, and is the only person who can take a store off a pan and put it into a flood channel in the same season
weaknesses: has no neutral state at all: every cup of either water moves him permanently toward an end, and there is nothing he can drink that undoes it
is capped at the eleventh gate by a vessel that is still split behind the sac, so no amount of practice will make him the body his range suggests he should be
is worth his standing for one shift at a time and is classified by a number the reach revises twice a season without asking him
cannot be assessed, promoted, or sent anywhere he would still be the same man, and has been moved once and did not survive the move as anybody's expectation
has no practice, no defence and no standing at all outside the channel, and is a poor, slow, frightened man on dry ground
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight here and it would be dishonest to describe one. He has no technique that reaches a man standing on a bank, and his one unbreakable advantage is worthless the moment the ground is solid. The only correct read is that nobody should be trying to fight him: the useful move is to need something from the section, and the only ways to get it are to wait for a shift or to push him, and the second one resolves the mixture and costs a season. Anyone who wants to break the reach's salt should break the man's rule about drinking before they break anything else, because a walker who has taken a cup of either water is a walker whose readings will start agreeing with the book again.
notes: The depth book records one water and his body contains two, so every reclassification since his first has been a bookkeeping event rather than a finding.
The suspended load he trains is not a bank. A bank can be spent once and then refilled; this mass has to be walked out, and the walking is the whole of his working life.
He has been asked twice to describe what he is and has given the same answer both times, which is the number of hours he can work before his own readings stop being usable.

art.palette_notes: Wet white, brine green and rust, and nothing else. The mixture dries in bands across him and the bands are the palette: chalk at the hems and elbows, translucent damp at the mouth and eyes, straw hair over a dark wet nape. The one saturated note is the rust bleeding out of the header wall he has leaned on for thirty years, and it is background, never skin. Light is hard overhead sun by day and bounce off a salt crust at night; there is no soft light source anywhere in his world. Ink contours fine and wet, wash laid in thin flat bands with the crust reading as opaque over the cloth rather than as a fill. No cast shadow on water.

identity.realm: No ceiling he can quote. He cleared a body gate on a routed load in his thirties and stopped, and what stopped him was not discipline but arithmetic: mass is meat and meat regrows on a fifty-year schedule, and reserve does not regrow at all, so every gate he ever reaches is one he spends rather than builds. He is also the only body on the heap that cannot use the basic defensive art of his own path.

appearance.presentation: A heavy, unhurried man who is warmer than the room and does not appear to notice. On the heap he reads as a piece of the ground that happens to be moving. Off it he reads as a man carrying something, which is usually correct. He gives the impression of great patience and of having already decided whatever was being decided.
appearance.age: Thirty-four on a span that runs to fifty, which is the arithmetic every emberblood is given and the only one he has ever been able to use. He has been on the Spoilwright's books for seventeen of those years, and the guild's own schedule assumes the other sixteen are still ahead of him, which they are, and also assumes they will arrive, which is a different claim.
appearance.build: Broad and thick through the back and the forearms, with a heavier trunk than a man who eats as little as he does ought to carry. Fire affinity in his body is structural rather than a gift, so the frame is permanently a little too warm and a little under-defended: his health is short of the ordinary mark and his bones are the heaviest part of him. The muscle is real, not qi, and every kilogram of it was paid for out of a fifty-year reserve with no way of being topped up.
appearance.complexion: Warm brown across the cheekbones and the ears with a sheen at the collarbone that is heat rather than oil, and it deepens over a shift and comes back over about an hour. Where his sleeves stop there is a hard line between flushed and not, and the line has not moved in seventeen years even though his seasons have. He does not sweat under load in the way other men do; he dries from the outside in.
appearance.hair: Cropped hard because a longer head holds a hat full of its own heat, and grey at the temple already, which on this body is not vanity but arithmetic. He cuts it himself and cuts it too short, and the guild's foreman has stopped offering him the loan of a decent pair.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary, deep-set and slightly too quick, which is the one speed in him that is not structural. An emberblood reads intent at the speed of a struck match; he has learned to sit on that, and the effort shows as a deliberate slowness in the eye rather than in the body.
appearance.palette: Soot, rust and hot iron. Everything he wears is grey-black with the hem singed in a ragged line at exactly the height the heap radiates, so his silhouette carries its own scorch mark wherever he goes. The one warm note in any frame is his own skin at the collar and the cuffs. Nothing about him glows; he is hotter than the ground, not lighter than it.
appearance.attire: Three layers of heat-dissipating undercloth worn under a borrowed guild coat two sizes too large, because the discipline this body should be wearing judges the fit of the inner layer and he is the only man on the heap not in the discipline. Sleeves tied at the elbow before a shift and never let down. Soles ground flat by the heap rather than by any cobbler, and the coat hem singed because the coat is not his and has been carried on the heap before.
appearance.marks: Old burns across the knuckles and inside both elbows, dated by nothing, because he came to the work without ever having been taught the drills that would have dated them. A seam of grey-white bloom along the left ribs where a load has been set down repeatedly in the same place, and the skin there is thickened in a way the guild's physician has declined to certify as anything at all.
appearance.bearing: Low, square and unhurried, with the whole body apparently available for a fourth load. He does not straighten up at the end of a carry and he does not wince, and the impression of a man being careful with himself is entirely wrong: he is being careful with the arithmetic.

canon.role_in_story: Spatial law is unspent on the mortal plains, so spoil does not disperse. Forty years of heap still stands on ore that is gone, and it has to be moved by hand before the working face can advance a foot, which makes it the last job on the tier that nobody has found a cheaper way to do. The Spoilwright is the guild that moves it, and its carriers die on it at a rate the guild records and does not discuss. The arithmetic is plain and nobody likes it: a carrier who can hold a load inside himself never has to set it down, and the only body in the setting that can do that is a furnace body, whose fuel is its own tissue and whose span is fifty years. So the guild buys the fast bodies and loses them. He is the one carrier on the heap who has found the other half of that arithmetic. An emberblood's fire refines faster than anything on the plains, and fire affinity is structural rather than a gift, so the fuel is not scarce and the tissue is: every elemental discharge is paid in flesh, and flesh is the one resource in this arrangement that grows back. He therefore keeps the fire out of his technique entirely and pays out of mass instead, which is slower, which is why he takes four hours where his guild-mates take one, and which is the only reason he is the guild's longest-serving carrier instead of its most recent one.
canon.first_appearance: First seen coming down the face of the heap at a walking pace with empty hands, stepping around two places where the ground has already stopped being floor, and answering the question of how a man can take four hours over a load his guild-mate took in one by asking the asker what they would rather he did with the difference.
canon.lore: An emberblood refines faster than anything on the plains and dies in decades, because no elemental law is seated beneath it on this tier to burn into, so it eats its own reserve as fuel. That single arithmetic is the whole reason the Spoilwright has a casualty column and the whole reason the discipline that would answer it does not work on him: the Quench Order teaches deliberate spending of a furnace before it overflows, and the technique assumes the furnace asks a question, and his has never asked for anything. On the body path, an emberblood's problem is that the setting's cheapest fuel is the setting's most expensive body. Tiger Palm is a short palm driven off the heel with nothing elemental in it at all, every point of its output raw body mass, so no element matchup can blunt it. He uses it exclusively and refuses to put fire into a strike at any gate, which reads to every instructor he has ever met as a man failing to see an obvious advantage. The counter is arithmetic: mass is meat and meat regrows on a fifty-year schedule, and reserve does not regrow at all. The second half of it is worse. Carapace Form hardens the outer frame until qi runs along it like wire, and it is half elemental, so it holds against wood and cracks against fire, which means the basic defensive art of his own path is the one thing on the heap that cannot be used by the one body on the heap made of fire. He has no shell. He is the heaviest carrier on the face and the only one who goes out in the open in anything less than a guild coat, and there is no version of that which is going to change, because the element that would harden him is the element he is.
history: Took the Spoilwright's term at seventeen because it was the only work on the tier that did not ask him what he intended to do with his life, and discovered in the first season that a carrier is paid by the load and a furnace body is paid by the hour, so the money and the body disagree from the first week.

Was put to the carapace drill at twenty-one as every guild apprentice is, and broke his own form inside a month, which is the only recorded instance on the heap of the technique failing against the practitioner's own element rather than against a wielder's.

Worked out at twenty-four that an unelemental palm costs meat instead of reserve and takes four times as long, and has never once put the reasoning in writing, because the guild pays by the load and a written reason would be a conversation about wages.

Carried his father off the same heap at thirty-one, in four hours, up a slope, and has never described the four hours to anybody, and settled the whole question of which resource he was willing to spend on that afternoon.

Was offered a term at the working face, where the material is dense rather than heavy, and refused it in one sentence: the face is a place a body gets better at and the heap is a place a body gets used up, and by then he had a clear enough idea which one he was standing on.

personality.summary: Enormously slow to hurry and entirely without illusions about being hurried, courteous in the flat way of a man who expects to still be here in ten years, and privately contemptuous of any discipline that produces a better number by spending something the guild does not pay for.
traits: patient to the edge of other people's patience and completely unbothered by it
publicly slow, privately exact about the difference between his two resources
loyal in the specific sense that he will still be standing where he was put after the person who put him there has gone
cannot be impressed by an advantage, and says so once and then never again
mannerisms: sets a load down in the same place every time, and has worn the seam into his own ribs doing it
rolls his shoulders once before a carry rather than flexing, and does it before anybody is looking
ties his sleeves at the elbow and leaves them tied through the whole shift including the meal
answers an argument about technique by asking who is paying for it
steps around the places where the ground has already stopped being floor, always, and never explains why
motivations: to reach the last gate his span will support without spending the reserve he has no way of replacing
to be paid for the load he actually moves rather than the load he is judged on
to see the face advance a foot that he has personally made safe to stand on

personality.voice: Low, slow, and almost entirely made of procedure. He answers an abstract question with a specific one. He has exactly one sentence for his own kind of work and repeats it, and he has never once used it to win an argument.

relationships.note: A fire-affinity body that runs hot and short, refines faster than anything here and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, with a lifespan measured in decades. Fire affinity is structural rather than a gift, which is the entire reason the reserve can neither be trained up nor argued with, and why a discharge is paid in flesh rather than in effort.

Elemental law is unwritten on this tier, so a fire affinity here has nothing beneath it to spend into and has to draw on its own reserve instead. That is not a weakness somebody chose and cannot be trained away; it is the ground effect, and he is the version of it that walks and carries.

The guild that moves the spoil heap off the seam floor, which is the only remaining ore-costly job on the plains, because spatial law is unspent and forty years of heap has to be carried out by hand before the working face can advance a foot. It pays by the load, it records its casualties, and he is the only carrier on the books who is still on the books.

A short palm driven off the heel with nothing elemental in it at all, every point of its output raw body mass, so no element matchup can blunt it. He uses it exclusively and refuses to let fire into a strike, because mass is meat and meat regrows on a fifty-year schedule while reserve does not regrow at all, which is a slower art bought with the only resource this body actually has.

It hardens the outer frame until qi runs along it like wire, and it is half elemental, so the form holds against wood and cracks against fire. His element is fire, so the basic defensive art of his own path is the one thing on the heap that cannot be built on him, and the guild has had no answer to that since the day he broke it.

Forty years of cutting down to stone that pays nothing, with the spoil heap still standing on the ore that is gone. Spoil does not disperse where spatial law is unspent, so exhaustion is visible from outside and a resource can be seen to have been spent out rather than suspected to have been, which is the whole reason the work still exists to be done by hand.

reference_stats.summary: The heaviest carrier on the heap, working at a third of the speed of the men beside him, on a body that cannot be defended and cannot be refuelled. Everything he does is paid for in tissue rather than in qi, and the tissue is the only resource he has any mechanism to replace. He is nearly unkillable in a grinding attrition and nearly helpless in a fight, and he has arranged his entire working life around that sentence.
strengths: takes a load into his own frame and does not set it down, so he never has to find a second pair of hands for the part of the path where nobody else is working
pays every effort out of mass instead of reserve, which means he can keep going long past the point where a furnace body that spends qi has to stop and recover
has the heaviest bone and the densest frame on the heap and hits harder than anything his own guild teaches, because the technique he uses has no element in it for anything to blunt
knows the face well enough to step around the places where the ground has already stopped being floor, which has kept him off the casualty column for seventeen years
is the only carrier on the books whose arithmetic can be reproduced by anybody who wants to check it, which nobody has ever done
weaknesses: cannot build a carapace, so the one defensive art of his own path fails against him rather than for him, and he goes out on the open face in a borrowed coat
has no ceiling he can quote and no reserve he can bank, so every gate he ever reaches is one he spends rather than builds
is slower than every other body on the heap by a factor the guild records and prices, so his standing depends entirely on there being nobody left who is faster
carries a body whose health is below the ordinary mark and whose span is half his parent's, and has made no plan for the last decade of it
has no defence that works at all against anything elemental, and his own element is the most common elemental on the plains
reference_stats.combat_read: There is a fight here and it is a bad one. He wins by being the last one standing in a place that grinds people down, because the technique he uses has no element matchup to read and no qi bill to run out of, and he loses instantly to anything that decides to be fast. The honest read is that he is not the threat in any engagement — he is the reason a face advances a foot. Anyone who wants him out of a position should make the position untenable rather than make him lose it, because he cannot be made to lose it and will simply be standing there at the end of it, carrying, on a span that is measured in decades and is already eleven years spent.
notes: The guild pays by the load. Every argument he has ever had about his method is an argument he has declined to have in writing.

The burn marks on his knuckles were never dated by a drill, because he was never taught the drills that date them; the discipline on this ground judges its practitioners by the calendar written on their skin and he is not in it.
The seam along his left ribs is where he has set down several thousand loads in the same place, and the guild's physician has declined to certify it as an injury.

art.palette_notes: Soot, rust and hot iron. Three values and no fourth: grey-black cloth, rust-brown spoil, and the single warm note of his own skin at the collar and the cuffs. Light is grey overcast on the face and hard sun on the open heap, never both in one frame. No glow, no emission, no inner light: he is hotter than the ground, not lighter than it. Ink contours heavy and confident, wash flat and opaque on the cloth, transparent on the spoil so the ore shows through the dust.

identity.realm: A body gate cleared in his thirties on a routed load, and then nothing, and the nothing is not a shortfall. His subspecies replaced a fungal colony with a mineral lattice that holds qi rather than transacting with it: the frame does not tire and nothing in it is being repaired, so a load put into him stays in him and the same lattice that let him clear the gate is the reason he has forty years of life left rather than two hundred.

appearance.presentation: A big, unhurried man in a household's soft clothes, who looks for exactly as long as he is listened to and then stops. He gives the impression of being simple until he says a number, at which point it is the right number and the impression is spent. Carried on his shoulders and along his forearms is a fine grey dust that is not cave dust and does not come off.
appearance.age: Thirty-eight on a span that runs to ninety, which is three quarters of what his parents had and one whole lifetime of somebody else's habit to rebuild in. He has been the household's carrier for twenty-seven of those years and has been re-taught twice, because the household was rebuilt twice inside that time, and both rebuilds had to start with him rather than with the stores.
appearance.build: A lanternfolk frame with the fungus gone: heavier than it looks and denser through the long bones than a man of his height ought to be, with a chest that does not rise and fall as much as a body should and forearms that have not tired in front of anyone since he was nineteen. The mineral lattice sits under the ribcage and along the spine as a fine silver-grey line rather than as a mass, and it is the reason the frame does not fatigue and the reason nothing in it is being repaired.
appearance.complexion: Chalk-pale and cool, faintly translucent at the temple, and it does not blanch under strain the way a living body's does. He looks ill indoors and well out of doors, because indoors the only warmth available is other people and he cannot take any of it. After a carry he is paler rather than flushed, which is the single clearest sign of his subspecies and the reason a house that has never seen one has trouble believing the description.
appearance.hair: Thin, pale and dry, and it comes out in handfuls rather than strands. He has decided that a shaved head is a form of accounting rather than of vanity, on the grounds that a household cannot count what it cannot see, and he has been shaving it for most of a decade.
appearance.eyes: Ordinary human vision, and better than ordinary in the dark: unlike his parent species he sees without a lamp at all, which is the single most-cited difference between the two bodies and the reason this one is named for it. The eyes themselves are unremarkable and completely unrevealing, which on his ground is its own kind of useful, since the survey culture treats anything seen as provisional until somebody has heard it.
appearance.palette: Cave grey, wet stone and one small warm note: the lamp-coloured skin of his own hands, which is the only light-coloured warm thing in any frame he is in. Everything else is the folded bedding of a limestone range — cold, banded, and carrying the same grey dust his shoulders are permanently coated in. The pale lichen ring that marks a held trial is never near him, and the absence is the point of the picture.
appearance.attire: Soft, close and quiet, with hard soles for working surfaces, cut by his own household in the local manner and worn until the hems are grey to the elbow. No buckles anywhere, because a buckle is a thing that catches on a bedding cleft. A wide belt of plaited cord carries nothing at all, which on his ground is conspicuous, and the cord is knotted in a shape his household uses and he cannot explain.
appearance.marks: A fine mineral line around the sternum and a second one running the length of the spine, silver-grey and very slightly proud, where the bloom nucleated across the wound the failed colony left behind. The sternum line has not changed in size or colour since he was nine. Below it, a band of thickened skin across both forearms and across the top of the shoulder, which is a load mark rather than an injury and which has not moved in nine years.
appearance.bearing: Still, heavy and unhurried, with the patience of a body that has never had a reason to hurry and no reason to believe it will need to. He stands where he has been put and waits to be told, and then does it in one trip.

canon.role_in_story: The household he belongs to keeps no stores and times its year against an animal, which is the practice every hearthborn household on the plain has for four generations and the only reason a household that averages whatever it takes in survives being moved. Averaging is a slow mechanism: it rebuilds a line in a generation rather than funding one exceptional child, and it is dependable rather than strong, and it needs somebody to carry things. The caves cannot be moved but everything in them has to be moved up the bedding before the herd season, because the only level with air is the one the herd uses, and a household that keeps no stores has nothing to fall back on but the backs of its members. He is the member the household cannot do without and cannot replace, because his subspecies replaced a fungal colony with a mineral lattice that holds qi instead of transacting with it, and a lattice does not tire and does not renew. That is the whole of his usefulness and the whole of his limit: a frame that carries a season's stores up a bedding in one trip and repairs none of it, in a body with ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty. It is also the whole of his invisibility. Lichen colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it, and it never washes off, and it is the only reliable record in the setting that a trial was held. He has walked the same bedding thirty-one times carrying more than a man should and the stone has never once come up marked, because a lattice holds rather than transacts, and the survey culture whose entire ethic is that a figure is provisional until somebody has heard it therefore has no figure at all for the largest single act of labour in its territory.
canon.first_appearance: First seen carrying a household's whole season up the bedding in one trip, and when asked how much that was, naming the four households he has carried for rather than giving a weight, and then adding that nobody will be able to check the number afterwards because the stone he walked has come up clean.
canon.lore: A deadlight is a lanternfolk whose fungal colony died and was colonised in the wound by a mineral bloom able to survive the same conditions. The colony transacted with qi; the bloom holds it, which is structurally different and structurally unconstrained by the colony's limits, and it cost the subspecies two hundred and fifty years and gave back the mind path their parent had outsourced away. A bloom renews nothing, so nothing in this body is being repaired: he eats far more than a lanternfolk, has a health mark below the ordinary one, and carries fifteen percent less capacity than an ordinary frame while reading thirty percent better than one, which is the subspecies' whole bargain in a sentence. The body path was available to the parent and was found slow, and it is available here for the same reason: what the tree calls loading is precisely what a lattice does, and what it costs a living frame is fatigue, which he does not have. So the discipline he has built is not a hardening art but a routing one — the load goes into the lattice and not into the muscle, because the lattice does not tire, and a lattice that does not tire also does not heal, which means a load put into him stays there and he has been putting the same loads in the same place for nine years. On the body path the setting offers him a defensive drill he cannot use: Carapace Form hardens an outer frame until qi runs along it, and he has no outer frame in the sense the drill requires, only a boundary that is part of what he is. What he practises instead is Iron Skin, which drives qi into the fascia until the skin stops being soft, and which is the cheapest version of the same idea and the only one his ground will let through. The line he carries is a hearthborn: the most ordinary concentration in the setting, held for four generations by a household that has repeatedly taken in people it had no room for and averaged them in, so that it is dependable rather than strong and has never once been strong. It is the reason the household can be rebuilt twice in twenty-seven years. It is also the reason nobody can say what he is, including him, because the only true answer is that he is the average of everyone the house has ever held, and the house has held four households' worth of people who never shared a grandmother.
history: Born into the fourth averaging of a household that had already taken in twice, so his parents' concentration was assembled rather than inherited, which is the mechanism a hearthborn line actually runs on and the reason the grant is small and steady and never anything else.

Put to carrying at eleven, because a lattice takes a load at any age and the household keeps no stores and had no other member old enough to get a season's worth up the bedding before the herd turned.

Worked out at sixteen that he leaves no lichen anywhere he has carried, told nobody for six years, and then told the household anyway on the grounds that a house which cannot be checked is a house that has no claim anybody else can be obliged to respect.

Cleared a body gate in his thirties on a routed load and stopped there, having worked out that the same lattice that let him clear it was the reason he would have forty years of life left instead of two hundred, and that those were not two facts but one.

Was offered the trial the March charter's line owes its vacant seat — a trial nobody in the line has ever been put to — and refused it, because the one asset his body has is that it cannot be judged, and he will not spend it on an office that has stood empty for two generations as a piece of arithmetic.

personality.summary: Enormously strong, extremely slow to be hurried, and privately aware that the one thing he is good at is the one thing nobody can check. He is good company and an unreliable narrator of himself, because no instrument has ever returned a reading about his work and he has stopped inventing one.
traits: patient to the point of appearing incurious, which is a function of never having needed to hurry and not of any lack of attention
exact about what he can and cannot carry, and completely unable to estimate what he can carry
evasive about his own lineage in a manner that is mistaken for modesty and is actually a refusal to guess
scrupulous about other people's loads and careless about his own body, in that order, always
mannerisms: tests every surface with his heel before he brings a load down onto it
counts the households he has carried for when asked how much he carried, and does not notice that he has changed the question
comes to a halt in the middle of a sentence when a figure is wanted and resumes without embarrassment when nobody insists
wipes his hands on his thighs before touching anything belonging to somebody else, which nobody on his ground can explain and all of them do
walks with his shoulder against the wall on any surface that will take it
motivations: to be measured once by somebody who does not belong to his household and will not benefit from the answer
to carry the household's last averaging into a generation that outlives him, which is a shorter sentence than it sounds and the whole of his work
to leave a mark of some kind on some surface, once, before the span runs out
flaws: has no way of estimating his own strength and has never attempted to, which means every offer of more is genuinely tempting
treats being unverifiable as an inconvenience rather than as the arrangement that has built his entire life
will not say his household's name first in a hall, and cannot explain why, and has never once been asked to
personality.voice: Slow, warm and entirely made of concrete nouns. Answers a question about a body with a number and a question about a person with a story. He has exactly one phrase for what he is and uses it far too often, and when somebody else uses it first he goes quiet for the rest of the conversation.

relationships.note: A lanternfolk body with a silicate lattice where the hyphal colony was: lighter, colder and entirely inert, ninety years instead of two hundred and fifty, fifteen percent less capacity and thirty percent more insight, and nothing in it is being repaired because a bloom renews nothing. What the colony did for the parent and what it prevented can both be measured on this body, and the only practical result of that measurement is a set of hands that cannot get tired.

The most ordinary concentration in the setting, carried carefully for four generations and averaged with whatever the household took in, so that the line is dependable rather than strong and rebuilds itself in a generation rather than funding one exceptional child. He is its whole living evidence and its only proof that the mechanism works, because the household has been rebuilt twice inside his working life and both times started with him.

A people who measure a life by how many of the realm's gates were already closed when they were born, which takes the whole ladder as arriving late by definition. This subspecies is the extreme case of that measure: every path open, three quarters of a parent's lifespan, and no way to spend a century getting ready, which is precisely the arithmetic that makes his ground measure him in shifts instead of in seasons.

It colonises worked stone wherever a large quantity of qi has been drawn through it and it never washes off, which makes it the one record in the setting that cannot be edited by whoever lost. A colony transacts with qi and a bloom holds it, so the stone he walks stays clean; thirty-one carries up the same bedding and there is nothing on it, and the absence is the only thing anybody has instead of a figure for the largest single act of labour on that ground.

It drives qi into the fascia until the skin stops being soft, and reads as blunt force taken rather than a strike dealt. It is the cheapest version of the body's basic hardening art and the only one his ground will let through, because the expensive version needs an outer frame to harden and what he has instead is a boundary that is part of what he is rather than a covering over it.

A loading routine for the long bones: denser skeleton and better muscle fibre, so a practitioner who trains it hits harder and still does not cast qi. It is the only loading art on his path that is honest about what it produces, and on a lattice frame it does not tire, so the routine is not a discipline he maintains but a condition he has.

reference_stats.summary: The strongest body in his household by an order of magnitude, on a frame that does not tire and does not heal, and the least measurable man on ground whose whole ethic is that nothing counts until it has been heard twice. He can move a season's stores in one trip and cannot tell you what a season's stores weigh. Everything he is survives; almost nothing he does can be proved.
strengths: carries a lattice frame that does not fatigue, so a load held by him is a load nobody has to set down twice and a shift's work is a shift's work rather than a shift's work in instalments
sees in the dark without a lamp at all, which on his ground is the difference between a figure and an unmeasured place
routes load into the mineral lattice instead of the muscle, so nothing he does is paid out of qi and his technique costs him no reserve he cannot replace
reads thirty percent better than an ordinary frame and reasons entirely unmediated, because nothing occupies his interior to answer a question before he has finished asking it
has ordinary human fertility and roughly four times the parent's gestation rate, which makes his subspecies the only way the caverns have found to keep a lanternfolk-shaped body in them at all
weaknesses: lives ninety years and repairs none of it, so a load put into his lattice stays in his lattice and there is no mechanism at all for taking one out
carries fifteen percent less capacity and less health than an ordinary frame, so a big enough load will still stop him and there is no training that changes the ceiling
cannot be assessed by the one instrument his ground trusts, and has therefore never been promoted, ranked, licensed or credited with anything he has actually done
eats far more than a lanternfolk and cannot leave the caves, so a bad season is a bad season at both ends at once
has refused the one trial his line owes a vacant seat and has no arrangement at all for what the seat does next
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no fight here and it would be dishonest to invent one. He has the densest frame on his ground and a hardening drill that works, and against anything that must move through a wall of him he is close to immovable. Against anything that decides to be fast, he loses before it starts, because a body that carries and never hurries has no answer to a strike it never saw coming. The correct read is that he is not a combatant and should not be deployed as one: he is the reason a household survives a relocation, and the useful move against him is never to fight him but to move something he has promised to carry.
notes: The sternum line has not changed in twenty-nine years and no physician on his ground will discuss it, which is the only subject on which the entire household is silent.

He has walked the same bedding thirty-one times and the stone has never come up marked, which he regards as a property of the work rather than as a fact about himself and has been argued out of twice.
He carries a hearthborn line and cannot say what that is, and the only answer available to him is a list of four households whose members shared no ancestor he can name.

art.palette_notes: Cave grey, wet stone, and one small warm note: his own hands and the skin of his face, which is the only warm light-coloured thing in any frame he stands in. Limestone bedding is the background for everything, banded and cold, and the grey bloom dust on his shoulders and forearms is a slightly different grey from the rock so the silhouette separates without any outline. The lichen is never allowed in the frame: there is none, and that absence is the point of the picture rather than a simplification of it. Light is a single carried lamp or shuttered daylight, so every frame has one source and a large dark side. Ink contours fine and slightly uncertain, as if laid twice; wash laid in thin cold layers, transparent in the shadow half so the bedding reads faintly through him.

identity.realm: Mind path, walled and still, and the wall is not a discipline he chose. His body path is closed outright and the closure is not a prohibition but an outcome: a cinderkin that attempts it disperses and re-forms smaller. So the whole of his cultivation is the negative of growth — a practice of holding one shape in a species whose only way of growing is to come apart — and the techniques available to him are surface techniques, because he has a boundary and no frame, a core and no fascia.

appearance.presentation: A person-shaped absence of light with a person's habits. On a terrace of cut stone he is the one figure whose shadow is his own shape and whose outline does not flicker. He moves like someone who has thought carefully about the order of his limbs, because he has — a cinderkin has no muscles, and the lanes that hold a shape are the only thing between an intention and the air. He is the warmest thing on any of those nine terraces and the only one who casts no heat onto the stone.
appearance.age: Ageless in the way the setting's elemental bodies are ageless, which is not the same as undated: he has been on the Court's high ground since the ley last resolved to fire, and the only count anybody keeps for him is the number of vacancies he has waited out, which is nine years and rising. Nothing in him is ageing. That is the fact he works with most often and least comfortably.
appearance.build: A stable flame with a consistent silhouette: a core, a boundary, and a set of convection lanes that hold a shape. There is no mass to speak of and no fixed quantity of it, so he is the same height on every measurement and a slightly different weight on each. He has no organs, no limbs in the muscular sense, and a body that grew nothing and lost nothing, which is why he wears more clothing than anyone else on the terrace and why the clothing does not fall the way clothing is supposed to fall.
appearance.complexion: Not applicable and he has stopped apologising for that. What a person sees is a translucent fire with a dark core and a bright edge, the interior shifting continuously and the outline holding, so that a still photograph of him is always slightly wrong about the middle of him and never wrong about where he ends.
appearance.hair: A crown of standing flame, blue at the root and going up through straw to a colour that has no name for what it looks like on the high ground. It moves when he moves and does not move when he does not, and it has never once gone out, including in the flood.
appearance.eyes: Two places where the interior reads brighter than the rest, set at the height a face would put them, and they do not blink because there is nothing behind them to blink. They track a speaker accurately and a printed page not at all, which is the one limitation of his senses — temperature, fuel and flow, and no other channel — and it means he has never read anything.
appearance.palette: Fire, and the specific fire of a law slot seated in heat: deep core, blue shoulder, straw edge, on limestone cut grey. Against nine terraces of cold cut stone he is the only warm value in the frame, which is exactly why the district is organised around him and exactly why nobody has appointed him to anything. Every frame must show what is lighting him and must not show him lighting anything.
appearance.attire: Court dress over a fire: a high collar, long sleeves and covered shoulders, because the standing instructions on that ground require a figure that can be checked quickly and because a cinderkin has no skin to be cold. The cut is heavy and the cloth hangs without obeying it, since there is nothing underneath for a garment to hang on. Everything is kept dark and matte so the figure stays the light source and nothing competes with him.
appearance.marks: None. There is no surface on him to hold one, which is the single most conspicuous fact about him in any room of people who mark themselves and each other for everything, and the reason the terrace staff have quietly adopted a private shorthand for him rather than a name.
appearance.bearing: Utterly still, and still in a way that reads as attention rather than as a stance. He does not settle his weight, because he has none to settle, and he holds a position so precisely that after a few minutes people stop noticing him standing there and start noticing him still standing there.

canon.role_in_story: Every appointment in both polities passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and the rule was authored by an attempt that came very nearly to filling four vacant immortal seats by decree; its whole content is that the highest office may name a seat and may not take one. The Nine Seat Notary names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, and it names them on the cut terraces above the lower district, where the vacancies are physical — engraved absences visible from below, with the whole district arranged around the argument about who steps into one. Every trial that rule sends a candidate to is passed by a body that has nothing to store, because a cinderkin's qi is entirely in transit and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly and none of them can refuse. He came up to the Court to stand one. The rule has therefore made him the most eligible applicant in the setting and the only one who will never be examined, and those two facts are the same fact: the office's competence and its prohibition are the same clause, so a cinderkin is not kept out of an office by a judgement about him but by a category that was written before he was born and is, as far as anyone can show, correct. Nine years of standing on a terrace cut for a seat he is categorically outside of, holding the only thing his species can hold — a shape — and the whole of his cultivation is the discipline of not becoming what he becomes when pushed.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing on the fourth cut terrace with his hands open and no heat-mark in the stone under him, while the Notary reads a vacancy aloud three terraces down and does not look up, because the rule says the office is not able to judge what is standing on that stone.
canon.lore: A cinderkin is an elemental body that needs a slot in the world's elemental law to exist at all, which is why that law has a range rather than a switch: a world with no elemental slot has no cinderkin, and a world that spends its slot on cold produces a different body entirely. Its anatomy is a stable flame with a consistent silhouette — a core, a boundary, and convection lanes that hold a shape — and no organs, no muscular limbs and no fixed mass. It senses temperature, fuel and flow and nothing else. It has no young; under enough stress it sheds a spark that finds fuel and re-constitutes on its own, which is why the population tracks the world's elemental slot rather than any birth rate. Its qi has no organ to sit in and is entirely in transit, so nothing can be stored in one and nothing can be lost from one either, and every gate that asks for storage is answered instantly. The body path is closed outright, and the closure is not a prohibition: a cinderkin that attempts it simply disperses and re-forms smaller. So the mind is where the only growth is, and the mind is open and unusually clear because a body with no interior organs has nothing between an impulse and the air. What that gap actually costs is specific and it is the whole of his art. The body's entire vocabulary is the vocabulary of a surface — Carapace Form hardens an outer frame until qi runs along it like wire, Iron Skin drives qi into the fascia, every stance in the tree spends weight. He has a boundary and no frame, a core and no fascia, a silhouette and no weight, so not one of those techniques has anything to act on and the basic defensive art of a neighbouring path would disperse him rather than teach him. What is left is the surface work: Glare of Warding returns an attacker's own attention back along the line it arrived on, half light, strong against dark and indifferent to everything else, and a body whose entire nervous system is a heat differential in conversation with its surroundings is the best returning surface in the setting. Clear Mind Sitting is a daily discipline that empties the head before the day starts, and for him it is not a discipline at all but a description of what he already is. That is his gift and his deficit in one sentence: he was born warded, so nothing can be taught to him and nothing can be certified on him.
history: Constituted on the Court's high ground where the elemental slot is seated in heat, so he is one of the few cinderkins that was never carried down a shaft and re-kindled, and he has never once been to a tier where his species could not lawfully exist.
Came up to the Court at nineteen to stand the trial, on the reasoning — which he has never revised and no longer defends — that a trial he could not fail was a trial he would pass.

Was not examined. The naming office cannot judge an elemental body and the rule requires a trial it cannot judge, so the office's competence and its prohibition are the same clause and he was never a candidate, only a category.

Put Carapace Form to a tutor at twenty-four, the basic defensive art of the body tree, which hardens an outer frame until qi runs along it like wire. He dispersed, and re-formed smaller, and has no account of the interval beyond the fact of the shape afterwards, and the tutor's notes record the hour as a failure of attention.

Has sat the waiting floor for nine years and arrived, somewhere around the sixth, at the conclusion that the rule is the only thing standing between him and four vacant seats — and that the moment a mind discipline becomes legible enough to certify, the category stops being the reason and starts being the oversight.

personality.summary: Exact, unhurried and entirely without resentment, because resentment is weather and he has none. He answers questions precisely and at length and has never interrupted anybody, in a body whose entire sensory apparatus is a heat differential and whose entire interior is a thing that gets flattened before the day starts.

absolutely without fear, and has never had the opportunity to find out whether that is courage or an absence of the equipment for it
loyal, with a real attachment, to a procedure that has never once needed him

answers the question that was asked, then the one directly behind it, and never the one further behind that
stops talking the instant he is asked to stop, which nobody else on the terrace can do without visibly deciding to

It is also the thing that killed the Glasskin, which is the clearest evidence in the record that an element is a process and not an object.

The office that names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, and which exists because four vacant seats were very nearly filled by decree and the attempt taught the setting to write a vacancy as its own state rather than as a zero. He reads the vacancies aloud on the terraces he is not allowed to occupy, and the reading is the entire of his employment.

Every appointment passes a trial the naming office cannot judge, and the rule is the only thing between an elemental population and four vacant seats, because this is the one body in the setting that holds no office, cannot be judged and would satisfy an appointment instantly. He is not kept out by a judgement about him. He is kept out by a sentence written before he was born, and the sentence is correct, and there is no appeal from a category.

It returns an attacker's own attention back along the line it arrived on, and it is half light, so it is strong against dark and indifferent to everything else. A body whose entire nervous system is a heat differential in conversation with its surroundings is the best returning surface in the setting, and it is also the only thing about his condition that is a gift rather than a defect — which means nobody can teach it to him and nobody can certify it on him either.

A daily sitting that empties the head before the day starts, mental clarity and a sharper read on the room, and the cheapest passive in the codex. For every other body it is work. For him it is a description of what he already is on waking, which is why he has never been able to explain to the terrace staff what he does between the lamp being lit and the first reading of the morning.

Nine cut terraces on the Court's high ground, each sized for one office, and the ground the vacancies are observed on. The vacancies are physical: a seat nobody has ever filled is an engraved absence, visible from the lower district, and the whole district is organised around the argument about who steps into it. He has stood on the fourth of the nine for nine years and has never once put a foot on the engraving.

reference_stats.summary: Unassailable against almost everything and inapplicable to almost everything. He was born warded, cannot be taught, cannot be certified, cannot be given a store, cannot be given a body, and would satisfy any trial the setting could put to him without a moment's thought. He is the most eligible applicant in the setting and the only one who will never be examined, and he has made his peace with that in a way that nobody who meets him believes at first.
strengths: answers any gate that asks for storage instantly, because nothing in him is ever stored, so no trial, test or threshold in the setting can refuse him for want of capacity
returns an attacker's attention along the line it arrived on by constitution rather than by training, which is strong against anything dark and indifferent to the rest
carries no fixed mass and dispenses with no store, so nothing can be taken from him, searched in him, or lost out of him
reads temperature, fuel and flow directly and has no other channel, which makes him a flawless reader of anything that has been burning and a completely useless one for anything that has not
cannot be dispersed into anything but a smaller cinderkin, so he survives the sorts of pressure that end most bodies and re-forms at a cost measured in size rather than in life
weaknesses: cannot read a printed page, a diagram or a surface by sight, because his only senses are heat, fuel and flow, which makes him functionally illiterate on the ground that runs entirely on documents
disperses under enough pressure and re-forms smaller every time, so every serious fight is a permanent and quantifiable reduction and there is no discipline in the codex that addresses it

has no body tree at all: not one hardening, stance or loading technique in the entire body vocabulary has a surface to act on, so a cinderkin's closest legal path is also the only path with no curriculum
is refused every office in the setting by category rather than by judgement, so he has nine years of standing and nothing that a career could be built from
perishes in sustained deep water and has measured the depth at which that begins on a terrace above a district where the water is not deep
reference_stats.combat_read: There is a fight and it is entirely one-sided, which is the problem. Against anything dark he is very nearly untouchable: nothing has ever got inside his boundary, because there is no inside. Against anything with no attack at all he has nothing whatever — he has no strike, no technique he did not have at birth, and no way to be taught one, because there is nobody alive who can teach a cinderkin a surface discipline and no surface on him to practise it against. The honest read is that he should never be placed in an engagement at all. The single genuinely dangerous fact about him is that every fight costs him size, permanently, and the correct move against him is a single deep-water approach rather than anything a sword does.
notes: He has never been examined by anybody for any purpose, in nine years, and has stopped treating that as a wound and started treating it as a research question about who else has never been.
The tutor's note on the Carapace Form attempt records the hour as a failure of attention. He has read it and considers it the most nearly accurate document ever written about him.
He reads the vacancies aloud every morning on a terrace he is not permitted to occupy, and the terrace staff have adopted an initial for him in their own records and have never explained it to him.

art.palette_notes: One warm subject against cold cut stone, and no exceptions. Deep core, blue shoulder, straw edge, on grey limestone: he is the only warm value in every frame and the only light source in the frame that is a person. Court dress is kept dark and matte so nothing competes with him, and the cloth hangs without obeying the cut because there is nothing underneath for a garment to hang on, which must read in every full-body frame. No cast shadow on the stone — that is a fact of his body, not a lighting convenience — and no glow cast onto surroundings, only contact darkening at the boundary. The interior is always in slow continuous motion and the outline is always absolutely still, so the two values move in opposition and the eye reads the edge as the person. Ink contour drawn as a single deliberate line at the boundary; interior wash laid in with no hard edge at all.
